Beat 1: **She danced in a cage as a go-go girl to pay rent, then won an Oscar for her very first major film.**

Beat 2: Born November 21, 1945, Goldie Hawn turns 81 today, originating from Washington, D.C.

Beat 3: Dropping out of college to teach ballet and dance in New York go-go clubs, she struggled with debilitating stage anxiety.

Beat 4: Turning her infectious giggle on Rowan & Martin's Laugh-In into comedic gold, she stunned critics in Cactus Flower.

Beat 5: Winning the Best Supporting Actress Oscar, she produced and starred in Private Benjamin, Overboard, and The First Wives Club.

Beat 6: Stepping back from Hollywood to raise Kate Hudson, Oliver Hudson, and Wyatt Russell alongside Kurt Russell, family always came first.

Beat 7: Founding MindUP to teach children emotional resilience worldwide, her sunshine spirit shines at eighty-one.

Beat 8: **Was Private Benjamin, Overboard, or The First Wives Club Goldie Hawn's funniest movie?**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind Hollywood's sunshine icon:**
• Dropped out of American University to run a ballet school and work as a go-go dancer in New York.
• Won both the Academy Award and Golden Globe for Best Supporting Actress in Cactus Flower.
• Has been in a beloved Hollywood partnership with actor Kurt Russell since 1983.

Which Goldie Hawn comedy do you rewatch most: Overboard, Private Benjamin, or Death Becomes Her?
posts.reel_script: Before conquering Hollywood comedies like Overboard and Private Benjamin, a struggling young dancer was performing as a go-go girl in New York City just to pay her rent. Beat 1: **He worked as an orderly in a psychiatric ward, then co-wrote Ghostbusters and directed Groundhog Day.**

Beat 2: Born November 21, 1944, Harold Ramis would be 82 today, originating from Chicago, Illinois.

Beat 3: Working seven months at a Missouri mental hospital and writing joke columns for Playboy, he honed comedy at Second City.

Beat 4: Blending deadpan intellect with anarchic farce, he co-wrote National Lampoon's Animal House and directed Caddyshack.

Beat 5: Co-writing and starring as Dr. Egon Spengler in Ghostbusters and directing Groundhog Day made him a comedy titan.

Beat 6: Enduring a rocky sixteen-year estrangement from close collaborator Bill Murray, the two reunited tearfully shortly before Ramis passed.

Beat 7: Winning a BAFTA for Groundhog Day and inspiring Judd Apatow and Adam Sandler, his comedic legacy is immortal.

Beat 8: **Was Ghostbusters, Groundhog Day, or Caddyshack Harold Ramis's greatest gift to comedy?**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind comedy's greatest architect:**
• Worked for seven months at a psychiatric hospital in St. Louis right after graduating from Washington University.
• Co-wrote Animal House, Stripes, and Ghostbusters, and directed Caddyshack, National Lampoon's Vacation, and Groundhog Day.
• Won the BAFTA Award for Best Original Screenplay for Groundhog Day.

Which Harold Ramis classic is your all-time number one: Ghostbusters or Groundhog Day?
posts.reel_script: Before playing brilliant paranormal scientist Egon Spengler in Ghostbusters, a young Chicago writer worked seven months as an orderly inside a psychiatric ward. Teaming up with Bill Murray at Second City, he co-wrote Animal House and directed timeless classics like Caddyshack, Vacation, and Groundhog Day. Every modern comedy filmmaker owes him a debt of gratitude. Remembering him on his birthday, which classic is your favorite?
posts.reel_caption: Did you know Harold Ramis worked in a psychiatric ward before co-writing Animal House and Ghostbusters and directing Groundhog Day? What is your favorite movie of his? #HaroldRamis #Ghostbusters #GroundhogDay

Beat 6: Fearlessly choosing challenging indie projects like Saved! and Into the Wild over easy teen-idol fluff, she stayed fiercely independent.

Beat 7: Shining in Pride & Prejudice and releasing indie folk music, her fearless authenticity inspires fans worldwide.

posts.comment:
**The secret behind indie cinema's fearless survivor:**
• Lived in twenty-seven locations by age nine before moving to Las Vegas and Los Angeles.
• Filed for and won legal emancipation at age fifteen so she could manage her own acting career and finances.
• Played Lydia Bennet in Pride & Prejudice and Johanna Mason in The Hunger Games franchise.

posts.reel_script: Before stealing every scene as fierce Johanna Mason in The Hunger Games and Gretchen Ross in Donnie Darko, a young girl in Nevada moved twenty-seven times before turning nine, sometimes sleeping in cars. Which of her films is your favorite?
